newsitem.title: CANADA: BHP revises Canada diamond mining plan.
newsitem.headline: BHP revises Canada diamond mining plan.

text.p: Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd has revised the development plan for its diamond mine in Canada's Arctic so that the richer Sable kimberlite pipe would be mined in the first phase and the Leslie pipe delayed.

The change was included in a final feasibility study for the Lac de Gras diamond mine in Canada's Northwest Territories and was announced on Tuesday by BHP's joint venture partner Dia Met Minerals Ltd.

Dia Met chief financial officer Grant Miller said in an interview the change was made because the Sable pipe has a richer grade and will improve project economics early in the mine's life. "Leslie is still included in the plan. It just won't be included in the initial 17-year phase," Miller said.
The feasibility study covers the first 17 years of mining. During that time the Panda, Misery, Koala, Fox and Sable kimberlite pipes will be developed.
Miller said the companies still expect the mine to have a total life of about 25 years.
A BHP spokeswoman said the order of mining was revised in part because of Sable's higher value, estimated at US$63 per tonne of ore, over Leslie at US$28 a tonne.

The change was also made because BHP is more confident of the reserves for Sable. The valuations for Leslie were based on a sample of only 300 carats rather than the 1,000 carats that the company said was its preferred benchmark.
While Dia Met said Leslie would be developed later, the BHP spokeswoman said only that it was "not necessarily out of the plan of development. We need to do more sampling."

She said mine cost estimates were reexamined as part of the feasibility study but the final figures were the same as previous estimates. These were C$900 million to bring the mine into production and a further C$300 million to expand operations in the 10th year of mining.

She declined to give details on the other two pipes that BHP feels may have economic potential. The further five pipes that warrant more sampling have been proven to be diamond bearing but must be explored with large-diameter drilling.
Apart from the substitution of Sable for Leslie, all other major elements of the mine development plan, such as processing, tailings disposal and site reclamation plans remain the same.
Dia Met said the priorities for the next four months will be the completion of a permanent accommodation complex and the delivery of fuel and construction materials over a winter road to the site.
The winter road is now open, and in excess of 2,000 tractor trailer loads are scheduled to be shipped. Contracts for the major buildings and plant facilities have been awarded.

The workforce of the site will remain at about 250 people until the accommodation quarters are completed in April when the workforce will increase to about 800 people. Prestripping operations will begin in the spring of 1997.
